title: The Remote Work Shift
text:
Remote working has transformed the way many organisations operate. Consequently, employees who once commuted for an hour each day now spend that time on other activities. Nevertheless, the shift has not been without difficulties, as some managers struggle to monitor productivity.

Furthermore, the absence of face-to-face interaction can weaken informal communication. In contrast, teams that meet regularly in person often report stronger bonds. Ultimately, most firms are adopting hybrid models that combine both approaches.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what did employees who once commuted do with that time?
options: They began spending the time on other activities
They started moving to larger offices
They asked for longer lunch breaks

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what can the absence of face-to-face interaction weaken?
What can be inferred about managers from paragraph one?
options: They find it hard to measure how productive remote staff are
They have decided to stop remote working entirely
They prefer employees who commute long distances
They think office equipment is no longer needed

questions.text: What is the writer's overall view of hybrid models?
options: They are unpopular with most employees
They have been proven to end all communication problems
They are a practical compromise that keeps benefits of both approaches
They are likely to disappear within a year

paragraph_translations: Uzaktan çalışma, birçok kuruluşun işleyiş biçimini dönüştürdü. Sonuç olarak, eskiden her gün bir saat yol gidip gelen çalışanlar şimdi bu zamanı başka etkinliklere ayırıyor. Yine de bu değişim zorluklardan arınmış değil, çünkü bazı yöneticiler verimliliği izlemekte zorlanıyor.

Ayrıca, yüz yüze etkileşimin olmaması gayriresmi iletişimi zayıflatabilir. Buna karşılık, düzenli olarak yüz yüze buluşan ekipler genellikle daha güçlü bağlar bildiriyor. Sonuçta, çoğu firma her iki yaklaşımı birleştiren karma modelleri benimsiyor.
